status: Public-source evidence audit plus explicitly editorial validation proposal
method: Manually read official Steam stores and Steamworks documentation, an official developer announcement, and individual public SteamDB chart pages through the web reader. No bulk scraping or sales estimation.

definitions.sample: Five selected comparisons, not an exhaustive zombie-survival release cohort. No supply denominator or genre success rate is calculated.
definitions.englishStoreReviews: The English Reviews count and whole-number positive percentage displayed by the observed Steam store page; not all-language reviews or units sold.
definitions.steamDbReviews: SteamDB's displayed aggregate review count and raw positive-review share. This is not its adjusted SteamDB Rating and is not interchangeable with Steam's English-language score.
definitions.peakCCU: SteamDB's highest observed simultaneous Steam players, with its displayed UTC date; not unique players, reach, owners or copies sold.
definitions.checkedAt: Date the source was checked, not necessarily the publication date or an exact simultaneous live snapshot. Dynamic counts can change between requests.
definitions.milestone: A developer-reported number with original platform and time scope retained; not an independently audited financial result.
definitions.inference: Our interpretation of the cited evidence, not a causal attribution result or a developer statement.

comparables.title: Project Zomboid
comparables.role: Emotional reference: ordinary-person vulnerability and a home worth protecting

release.definition: Steam displays 8 November 2013 and still labels the game Early Access.

promises: House looting, crafting, barricades and a large persistent survival sandbox
Zombie sight and hearing, dangerous gun noise, illness and resource pressure
Solo and multiplayer; extensive accumulated systems and mod support
comparables.currentVersusPlanned: NPC survivors with relationships remain in the developer's 1.0 plans; do not count planned NPC scope as currently shipped.

steamDb.definition: Historical simultaneous-player peak and observed aggregate review counts, not owners or sales.
steamDb.caveat: The peak belongs to an established game first on Steam in 2013; it is not a 2026 new-launch outcome.

comparables.caveat: Its breadth is a player-expectation reference, not a feasible three-week feature checklist.

comparables.title: VEIN
comparables.role: Direct substitute: first-person zombie survival crafting already exists

release.definition: Steam explicitly lists its Early Access release date.

promises: Scavenge buildings, craft, farm, cook and fortify a home
Developer says multiplayer, combat, power and water systems are playable
A demo with a smaller region and lower skill cap is available
comparables.currentVersusPlanned: EA notes describe about 4 × 4 km currently playable. A 14 × 14 km map, NPCs, raiders, settlements and quests are future plans, with a roughly five-year estimate, not a guarantee.

steamDb.definition: Historical simultaneous-player peak and observed aggregate review counts, not owners or sales.
steamDb.caveat: A launch-era peak establishes activity for this competitor, not profitability or unpaid reach.

comparables.caveat: 'Project Zomboid, but FPS' is occupied positioning. A new game must distinguish the experience rather than only perspective and tags.

comparables.title: 7 Days to Die
comparables.role: Established first-person scavenging, crafting and defence reference

release.definition: Steam separately displays full and Early Access release dates.

promises: Open-world FPS, survival horror, tower defence and RPG
Looting, crafting, fortification and destructible construction
Large environments, vehicles and extensive progression

storeReviews.caveat: Steam flags one or more off-topic review periods and says those periods are excluded from the displayed score under the observed preferences.

steamDb.definition: Historical simultaneous-player peak and observed aggregate review counts, not owners or sales.
steamDb.caveat: The peak is from the July 2024 full-release period, after a long Early Access history.

reportedMilestones.claim: The current store description reports over 20 million copies sold.
reportedMilestones.definition: Undated developer marketing statement on the store.
reportedMilestones.caveat: Do not call this Steam-only sales, 2026 sales, launch sales, net copies or revenue.

comparables.caveat: Long-run audience scale does not estimate the odds for a new entrant.

comparables.title: Road to Vostok
comparables.role: Adjacent solo FPS survival reference; not a zombie game
comparables.perspective: First-person, single-player, map-to-map travel rather than one asserted continuous world

release.definition: Steam explicitly lists its Early Access release date.

promises: Grounded FPS survival, looting, shelter customization and trading
Cross a dangerous border into an optional permadeath region
A free demo and multi-phase development are part of the presentation
comparables.currentVersusPlanned: Store EA text estimates two to four more years. Some prose still describes pre-launch work; treat it as developer intent, not a fresh inventory of shipped features.

steamDb.definition: Historical simultaneous-player peak and observed aggregate review counts, not owners or sales.
steamDb.caveat: This adjacent success does not isolate demand for zombies, co-op, crafting or the proposed route mechanic.

reportedMilestones.claim: The developer reported over 250,000 copies sold on Steam in 'What's Next (Build 2)'.
reportedMilestones.definition: Developer self-report at that date, read in full in the official Steam news feed; direct announcement URL returned only a title/image in the web reader.
reportedMilestones.caveat: Gross/net refund treatment not specified. Not current lifetime sales, profit, or a causal marketing study.

comparables.caveat: Supports the existence of a solo FPS survival audience, not a three-week production benchmark.

comparables.title: HumanitZ

release.definition: Steam separately displays full and Early Access release dates; this is not a wholly new February 2026 game.

promises: Urban scavenging versus countryside hunting, fishing and farming
Crafting, vehicles, base fortification and survival pressures
Solo, co-op, PvE and PvP with dedicated servers

storeReviews.caveat: Fresh opened page replaced an older search snippet showing 4,322 reviews. Do not mix the snapshots.

steamDb.definition: Historical simultaneous-player peak and observed aggregate review counts, not owners or sales.
steamDb.caveat: A full-release-era peak after Early Access since 2023, not a clean new-IP launch cohort observation.

comparables.caveat: A shared theme can attract activity without uniformly strong satisfaction; review percentages alone do not explain causes.

constraintFacts.claim: Steam onboarding lists a 30-day interval between paying the app fee and releasing a game for a partner's first few titles.
constraintFacts.definition: Game-release eligibility measured from fee payment, not 30 development workdays.
constraintFacts.caveat: The docs phrase this for the first few titles, not every app forever. The provided sources do not explicitly resolve a new partner's demo eligibility under this interval; verify the actual Steamworks checklist or ask Steam support before promising a date.
constraintFacts.planningImplication: A new full-game release cannot be promised inside a three-calendar-week sprint if this wait starts on day one.

constraintFacts.claim: The full game's public Coming Soon page must be visible for at least two weeks before its release.
constraintFacts.definition: A public store-presence interval, separate from fee payment and review time.
constraintFacts.caveat: Do not add 30 days and 14 days automatically; requirements can overlap. Do not transfer this rule to a demo's own optional upcoming page.

constraintFacts.claim: Store-page and product-build review each typically take 3–5 business days; Valve asks for at least 7 business days of planning allowance for each.
constraintFacts.definition: Typical review duration and recommended buffer, not a guaranteed service deadline.
constraintFacts.caveat: Submit a near-final build. Rework may be required. The dedicated Review Process page specifies business days; it is more precise than the shorter onboarding summary.
constraintFacts.planningImplication: For a day-15 Steam demo target, plan the near-final candidate and store preparation early, not on day 15. Day 8 is a proposed latest candidate target, not a Valve guarantee.

constraintFacts.claim: A demo has a separate App ID linked to its base game, its own configuration and review checklist. Before a pre-release demo goes live, the base game's store page must be public as Coming Soon.
constraintFacts.definition: A Steam demo is not releasing the commercial base app.
constraintFacts.caveat: The demo's own upcoming phase is explicitly optional: a fully reviewed demo can release directly to playable. This is not evidence that all new-partner onboarding constraints are waived.

constraintFacts.claim: After the first playable demo release, its owner can trigger one wishlist notification to base-game wishlisters within the first two weeks.
constraintFacts.definition: An optional once-only action, not automatic notification on every update.
constraintFacts.caveat: The documentation also describes a two-week wishlist-notification cooldown. An early rough public demo can consume a useful launch moment; a private prototype handoff is a separate deliverable.

constraintFacts.claim: Review checks require store screenshots to show gameplay and listed supported features to exist in the current build; future content must be clearly distinguished.
constraintFacts.definition: Product representation rules, not evidence that a prototype will pass review.
constraintFacts.caveat: Label one-street prototype footage honestly. Do not present a mockup, cinematic or unbuilt open world as shipped gameplay.

constraintFacts.claim: UTM Total Visits count visits with tagged URLs. Trusted Visits exclude bots/crawlers. Tracked Visits are signed-in visits with abnormal repeated traffic excluded.
constraintFacts.definition: Visits, not unique people or impressions.
constraintFacts.caveat: Report these denominators separately. Small campaign rows may be hidden by privacy thresholds; absence of a row is not zero demand.

constraintFacts.claim: Steam attributes wishlists, purchases and free-game/key activations to tracked UTM visits when the action occurs within 72 hours of the click.
constraintFacts.definition: Attributed store action within a fixed window, not proof that the link caused the action.
constraintFacts.caveat: Browser, device and app transitions can break attribution, although Steam's supported open-in-client/app banners can preserve it. UTM Analytics does not measure demo completion, route comprehension or voluntary replay; collect those separately with consent.

marketTheses.claim: There is demonstrated interest, but no empty 'FPS Zomboid' slot. VEIN directly combines the requested ingredients and has observed review/player activity; 7 Days to Die is an established first-person substitute.
marketTheses.definition: Competitive-positioning inference from selected released products.
marketTheses.caveat: This does not quantify market size, unmet demand, acquisition cost or startup success probability.

marketTheses.claim: Single-player is a credible slice to test: Road to Vostok's developer reports a substantial Steam sales milestone for a solo FPS survival game.
marketTheses.definition: Evidence for adjacent audience existence, not proof of demand for this game's zombies or hook.
marketTheses.caveat: A selected success with a long demo/development history cannot forecast a new team's three-week outcome.

marketTheses.claim: The largest risk is the gap between a mature survival-sandbox promise and a small team's deliverable. Narrow the demo to a repeated scavenging decision that changes the route home.
marketTheses.definition: Editorial production judgment based on comparable feature breadth.
marketTheses.caveat: No comparable supplies a reliable cost estimate for this team.

marketTheses.claim: A shortcut that helps carry loot home also gives infected a route to the safehouse. Test whether players recognize their own decision in the later threat and voluntarily try a different plan.
marketTheses.definition: Original synthesis for the proposed prototype, not a claim to have invented noise, persistence, doors or fortification.
marketTheses.caveat: Novelty, enjoyment and distinctiveness are unproven. An unexplained scripted ambush would not validate systemic consequence.

marketTheses.claim: These five examples support design comparison and demand existence only. Do not compute a Q2 hit rate or label their activity organic.
marketTheses.definition: Selected-case sample with no complete release denominator or controlled channel experiment.
marketTheses.caveat: No review-to-sales, CCU-to-owners, follower-to-wishlist or view-to-revenue conversion is made.
